name: Azzur
overview: Azzur is a male biblical figure noted as a non-Levite leader mentioned in Nehemiah 10:17. He is listed among the signatories of a sealed document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, indicating his role in a significant covenant or agreement during the post-exilic period. His tribal affiliation is not specified in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Azzur means 'help,' reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew context. There is no indication that this name was directly given by God, but its meaning suggests a role or characteristic associated with assistance or support.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Azzur as a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the broader Israelite lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azzur's importance lies in his inclusion among the leaders who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10, demonstrating his leadership and commitment to the community's religious and social reforms. As a non-Levite leader, his role highlights the involvement of various Israelite members in the restoration efforts following the exile. His mention underscores the collective responsibility embraced by Israelite leaders to uphold the covenant with God.
